newsitem.title: USA: SEC widens muni-bond "yield burning" probe - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: SEC widens muni-bond "yield burning" probe - WSJ.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission is broadening its probe of municipal-bond "yield burning" abuses to include Alex. Brown, the Wall Street Journal reported Thursday.

People familiar with the investigation said the SEC is also looking at Michael Lissack, the whistle-blower who sparked the initial investigation and a key witness in the SEC's examination of municipal-market abuses, the report said.

The paper reported that the SEC wants to know if Lissack participated in any abuses and also is examining Alex. Brown, the parent of Alex. Brown & Sons, which played a key role in two Pennsylvania deals that are now under scrutiny.
Yield-burning refers to accusations that bond underwriters overcharged issuers for U.S. Treasury securities bought in the open market and used in bond refinancing deals.
Other companies involved -- Merrill Lynch & Co, Smith Barney and Lazard Freres -- have said they've done nothing improper.
